A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same F2SA-p research, retaining the main complexity theorems and experimental benchmark. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 1 report original test-loss and accuracy results for learning regularization on 20 Newsgroup.

after.justification: Section 5 and Figure 1 report expanded original experiments, and Appendix G adds MLP results in Figure 2.

M1.justification: For odd p, Algorithm 2 replaces the forward-difference stencil j=0,...,p with j=-(p-1)/2,...,(p+1)/2 and different coefficients. This substantively changes the hyper-gradient estimator. Algorithms 1–3 also move stochastic sampling inside the inner iteration, specifying fresh samples at each step instead of sampling before the loop.

E1.justification: The empirical coverage remains the 20 Newsgroup learn-to-regularize task; no additional dataset is identified. The added MLP changes the evaluation model within that task. Data hyper-cleaning and reinforcement learning appear as illustrative applications, without reported experiments.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains F2SA, stocBiO, MRBO, VRBO, and the unregularized baseline. Figure 2 uses the same comparator set. Additional F2SA-p orders are variants of the proposed method, while newly cited methods are not added empirical baselines.

E3.justification: The evaluated orders change from p=1,...,5 to F2SA plus p=2,3,5,8,10, and Appendix G introduces a five-layer ReLU MLP evaluation. The stated regularizer also changes from ||W_x y||^2 to y^T W_x y while retaining W_x=diag(exp(x)), changing its parameterization. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V1 reports tuning p=1,...,5 but displays only F2SA and F2SA-2. V2 supplies explicit higher-order sensitivity curves and adds an MLP experiment testing behavior on a nonsmooth, nonconvex objective outside the main theoretical setting. This substantially expands the supplementary empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. Changes to stochastic algorithm sampling and theoretical expectations do not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds results for p=3,5,8,10 and changes retained trajectories, including F2SA-2. V1 reports p=2 as optimal, whereas v2's p=10 curve has the best final plotted loss and accuracy. Figure 2 adds MLP outcomes. These are revised or new iteration-based results, not established gains under identical settings or equal computational work.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1 and Appendix B replace the earlier coefficient-existence argument with explicit formulas and coefficient bounds, including an extended derivation for odd p. V2 corrects the even-order antisymmetry sign and states the lemma directly for vector-valued functions. Definition 2.1 adopts expected-gradient stationarity, and Lemma D.2 corrects its SGD update. The headline complexity rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The main upper-bound, lower-bound, and near-optimality contributions remain. V2 corrects the abstract's complexity expression to match the existing Theorem 3.1 and explicitly presents the finite-difference contribution as extending Chayti and Jaggi's meta-learning results and addressing their broader-applicability conjecture.

C2.justification: V2 removes the experimental explanation favoring p=2 because higher orders require more lower-level solves, and drops the broad dismissal of variance reduction. It instead proposes combining variance reduction or momentum with the method. New discussion connects high smoothness to logistic regression and presents the MLP experiment as evidence of potential beyond the theoretical assumptions.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses K=10 inner iterations and T=1000 outer iterations for the main experiment, identifies the unregularized baseline as SGD, specifies the MLP's depth, ReLU activation, and width 500, and supplies a reproduction-code link. The iteration counts are newly documented, not established increases over v1.

R1.justification: V2 acknowledges Chayti and Jaggi's earlier finite-difference connection and substantially revises the novelty positioning around extending that work. It also adds concurrent condition-number lower bounds by Ji and Chen and Zhang, cites finite-difference coefficient literature, and changes Table 1's lower-bound attribution from Theorem 4.1 to Arjevani et al.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and Appendices A–F remain recognizable. V2 locally rewrites introductory, methodological, and experimental passages, adds illustrative examples, acknowledgments, and Appendices G–H, and updates authorship. Much of the existing narrative is retained rather than comprehensively reorganized.

P2.justification: V2 adopts an ICLR conference layout throughout, changing typography, text width, headings, author blocks, and running headers. Figure 1 is redrawn with additional curves, revised colors, legend, axes, and caption; Figure 2 adds another two-panel display. Table 1 retains its basic structure.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is the strengthened finite-difference construction: v2 replaces odd-order forward coefficients, whose exponential growth it identifies, with an explicitly bounded alternative and develops the supporting derivation. Corrected sampling pseudocode and formal statements improve consistency, while prior-work attribution and expanded experimental evidence improve assessability. The plots still lack uncertainty reporting and equal-work comparisons, but the central mathematical and methodological repairs provide a substantial overall improvement.
